The course builds from the basics of grammar and structure of the English language, and goes on to include complicated rules as well, such as Modals, Conditionals, and so on. At the same time, I'm not sure if it was just me, or other students also experienced this, I did not come across any new structures or rules that I hadn't been exposed to before. But having the knowledge of these grammatical structures has indeed improved my reading and writing experiences. If you're an avid reader, you might have those moments where a particular sentence or the way it is phrased simply captivates you and you can't understand why, but this was a course that helped me understand what it was about those sentences or ways of writing that made them so alluring. I feel like this course could have done more to benefit literature students, perhaps by adding poetry, or writers with a dense writing style, to break their grammar down and explain how language can be used in varying ways. Rather, the course seemed to be focused more towards academic writing styles. But perhaps I was expecting too much from the course. Regardless, it did not feel like my time was wasted, and I doubt I missed any classes at all, for each class was a source of growth and learning.
